div.head: Wi 5
div.ab: Gif ðæs geweorþe gesiþcundne mannan ofer þis gemot, þæt he unriht hæmed genime ofer cyngæs bebod ⁊ biscopes ⁊ boca dom, se þæt gebete his dryhtne C scll' an ald reht.
Gif þæs geweorþe gesiþcundne mannan ofer þis gemot, þæt he unriht hæmed genime ofer cyngæs bebod ⁊ biscopes ⁊ boca dom, se þæt gebete his dryhtne C scll' an ald reht.
Gif ðæs geweorþe gesiþcundne mannan ofer þis gemot, þæt he unrihthæmed genime ofer cyngæs bebod ⁊ biscopes ⁊ boca dom, se þæt gebete his dryhtne C scƚƚ an ald reht.

Wenn es einem Mann vom [Kriegs]gefolgschaftsstande nach dieser [Staats]versammlung begegnet, dass er gesetzwidrige [Ehe-]Verbindung eingeht gegen das Gebot des Königs und Bischofs und der Bücher Spruch, der büsse das seinem Herrn mit 100 Schll. nach altem Recht.

If it happens to a man of the [military] retainer class after this [national] assembly that he enters an unlawful [marriage] union against the command of the king and bishop and the decree of the books, let him make amends for it to his lord with 100 shillings according to old law.

If after this meeting, a nobleman presumes to enter into an illicit union, despite the command of the king and the bishop, and the written law, he shall pay 100 shillings compensation to his lord, in accordance with established custom.

If after this meeting, any gesith-born man chooses to enter into an illicit union in spite of the command of the king and the bishop and the decree of the books, he is to pay to his lord 100 shillings according to ancient law.

If after this assembly [something] of this [nature] befalls to a gesiþ-born man, that he should take up an unlawful union against the king’s command and the bishop’s and the decrees of the books, he makes restitution for that to his lord with 100 shillings according to established right.

S. Gl Gefolgsadel 4a. Schmid 600a versteht nur Königsgefolge und unter dryhten (s. u. 9) nur den König. Doch hatte vielleicht auch mancher Magnat adliges Gefolge, hiess dessen Herr und empfing von ihm Strafgeld; s. Gl Gerichtsbarkeit 5—6c

See Gl Gefolgsadel 4a. Schmid 600a understands only the king’s retinue, and by dryhten (see below 9) only the king. Yet perhaps many a magnate too had a noble retinue, was called its lord and received fines from it; see Gl Gerichtsbarkeit 5—6c
Nicht Amnestie für frühere unkanonische Geschlechtsverbindung folgt hieraus, wie Schmid p. xxviii annahm, sondern im Ggs. zu blosser Exkommunikation für jene, fortan auch Geldstrafe
What follows from this is not an amnesty for earlier uncanonical sexual unions, as Schmid p. xxviii supposed, but, in contrast to mere excommunication for those, a money penalty as well from now on
S. o. Pro.⁹; Gl Witan 10
See above Pro.⁹; Gl Witan 10
Toller nimmt unrihthæmed als Ein Wort
Toller takes unrihthæmed as a single word
Nicht ‘pflegt’, sondern ‘sich einlassen in’ (z. B. Vertrag, Frieden), ‘take to’; Price
Not ‘practises’, but ‘enter into’ (e.g. a contract, peace), ‘take to’; Price

Kanonische Rechtsbücher, hier nicht nur Bibel; Schmid meint, Wi übertrage hiermit liber canonum, den Synode von Hertford 10 (vgl. Stubbs Councils III 121{e}) zitiert. Denselben Sinn hat domboc (Toller), boctæcing, boctalu; s. Wb. Vgl. Gl Eheverbot 1

Canonical law-books, here not only the Bible; Schmid thinks that Wi renders by this the liber canonum cited by the synod of Hertford 10 (cf. Stubbs Councils III 121{e}). domboc (Toller), boctæcing, boctalu have the same meaning; see Wb. Cf. Gl Eheverbot 1

Da dieses Eherecht höchstens zwei Menschenalter alt sein konnte, heisst eald wie Hl 12⁵ hier: ‘echt’. Die Summe erklärt sich wohl nicht aus Kenter Wergeld des Gemeinen, sondern eher als Verdoppelung der den Gemeinen treffenden Strafe in 5, 1

Since this marriage law could at most be two generations old, eald here, as in Hl 12⁵, means ‘genuine’. The sum is probably to be explained not from the Kentish wergild of the common man, but rather as a doubling of the penalty falling on the common man in 5, 1
The word gesiðcund, which is used in the Laws of Ine and Alfred, now takes the place of the antiquated word eorlcund, which is used in the earlier codes.
For the construction ðæs geweorþe cf. Beowulf, 1598, 2026, etc. Liebermann would emend to ðæt geweorþe.
The reference is presumably to ecclesiastical law—perhaps, as Schmid suggests, to those laid down at the Council of Hertford (cap. 10); cf. Bede, Hist. Eccl. iv. 5.

Liebermann suggests that eald cannot have its ordinary meaning here, since the provision cannot be more than two generations old. It may, however, denote what had already been established by custom, in contrast with an injunction ordered for the first time in a decree; or possibly the eald riht may refer to the amount of the fine to be paid to a lord for serious disobedience, without specific reference to this particular offence.

note.label: gesith-born
note.seg: This is the only occurrence in Kentish law of a term common in the West Saxon code of Ine, contemporary with Wihtred. It seems to refer to the same class which the earlier Kentish laws called eorlcund. The word gesith means “companion” and is applied in poetry and elsewhere to the members of a king’s comilutus. But it is clear from the term gesithcund “born a gesith” that it has come to denote a member of a class, and from Ine’s laws we find this had a wergild of either twelve or six hundred shillings. After the time of Alfred the six-hundred wergild disappears, and men of the twelve-hundred wergild are called thegns, not gesiths. A man of gesith rank was usually in charge of a household of his own, and it is in his capacity of lord of other men that he appears in Ine 23.1 and 50.

note.label: gesiþ-born
note.seg: According to Whitelock, English Historical Documents, 396: ‘This is the only occurrence in Kentish law of a term common in the West-Saxon code of Ine, contemporary with Wihtred. It seems to refer to the same class which the earlier Kentish laws called eorlcund. The word gesith means “companion” and is applied in poetry and elsewhere to the members of a king’s comitatus. But it is clear from the term gesith-cund “born a gesith” that it has come to denote the member of a class.’

note.label: books,
note.seg: Liebermann, Gesetze, 3:27 says this includes compilations of canon (church) law as well as the Bible.

note.label: right.
note.seg: Liebermann, Gesetze, 3:27 points out that this statute, with its reference to the bishop and (religious) books, could not be very ancient, and suggests translating ald, ‘old, ancient,’ along the lines of ‘established.’ This seems likely, as in any event the ‘ancient’ payments to the king for disturbance of public peace as laid out in Æthelberht §§8, 11, 12, and 14 was 50 rather than 100 shillings.
